memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the seventh day they must shave off all their hair; they must shave their head, their beard, their eyebrows and the rest of their hair. They must wash their clothes and bathe themselves with water, and they will be clean." - Lev 14:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything. Head, beard, eyebrows, the rest. Nothing left unshaved, nothing left unwashed. It is almost startling in its thoroughness.

And this is the second time. They had already shaved and washed on the first day. A week later, they do it all again.

God's cleansing is not casual. He does not deal with the obvious and leave the rest. When He restores a person, He does it properly — right down to the eyebrows.

We tend to want the quick version. Deal with the visible failure, tidy the surface, move on. But God is after something deeper than presentability. Create in me a pure heart, O God, David prayed — not a better reputation, but a new inner life (Ps 51:10).

That thoroughness can feel uncomfortable while it is happening. Being searched to the corners is not pleasant. But consider the alternative: a God who patched us up superficially and left the real damage untouched.

Our God is a consuming fire and a patient refiner. He will not stop halfway. Search me, God, and know my heart... See if there is any offensive way in me (Ps 139:23-24). That is a brave prayer, and it is safe to pray, because the One who searches you is the One who loves you most.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you settled for surface tidiness instead of real change?
2. What would it cost you to let God search you thoroughly?
3. Can you pray Psalm 139:23-24 honestly today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, do not let me settle for a tidy surface. Search me thoroughly, deal with what is hidden, and make me clean all the way through. Amen.
